description:
## Why
Elixir's `var!(v, Context)` (kernel.ex:4882-4900) lets two macros share one variable by naming a context explicitly. After fz-p8p.22, a quoted variable's context is `Macro(FunctionId, expansion ordinal)`, so there is no module-level context for two macros to share. fz-p8p.22 builds only `var!/1` (bind in the caller's context).

## What changes
Decide what a context name denotes in fz, for example the defining module with no ordinal. Then `var!/2` builds that context through the one var-node constructor. No fixture needs this yet. The first user is the fixture that proves it.

## Done when
A fixture has two macros sharing a variable through `var!(v, M)`, it runs on all three paths, and the macros guide documents it.
title: var!/2: a macro names the hygiene context a variable binds in
